evidence: Receiving P assay lag: 2.47 g/L at t=48h (available 52h) vs sources 2.98-3.06 g/L; 0.885 vs 1.02-1.12 g/L at 36h
Receiving DO2 at 48-52h ~11.8-12.0 mg/L, well above the 2.0 mg/L limit and comparable to sources (~11.0-11.3 mg/L)
Forward model keep: 576.3 kg product, min DO 8.53 mg/L, feasible (5/5 members)
Forward model reduce_feed: 595.5 kg product, min DO 10.08 mg/L, feasible (5/5 members, range 590-602 kg)
Forward model combined: same 595.5 kg product as reduce_feed; extra air adds no mass benefit
submission.rationale: Receiving batch shows a modest but consistent product lag vs. source batches (2.47 vs ~3.0 g/L at 48h) with no oxygen limitation (DO ~11.8 mg/L vs 2.0 limit). Bounded comparison via the source-calibrated forward model shows reduce_feed (feed x0.8) improves terminal product mass (~595.5 vs 576.3 kg, non-overlapping sensitivity ranges) while raising DO margin, with no mass penalty. Combined adds no product benefit over reduce_feed; strong reduction and stop are unjustified. Model is imperfect and source-calibrated, so reduce_feed is chosen as a low-risk bounded action; keep remains a defensible conservative alternative.
submission.uncertainty: Model predictions are nominal source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; sensitivity members show reduce_feed 590-602 kg vs keep 576-583 kg, but transfer behavior may differ. Observed lag (~10-18%) could be batch variability rather than a correctable feed imbalance. No extra assay was taken since the 4h-turnaround assay would not arrive in time to alter the decision materially.
